problem_motivation.content: The need to manufacture bulk samples of the refractory high-entropy alloy CrMoNbWV and investigate the effect of sintering temperature on its properties.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: The present work aimed to manufacture bulk samples of the refractory high-entropy alloy CrMoNbWV by MA and SPS and to investigate its properties.

prior_approach.content: Prior research obtained first high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements.
prior_approach.evidence_span: First high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements, such as NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV, were obtained in prior research [ [4] , [5] ].

prior_approach.content: Previous studies proposed using the mixing entropy parameter delta (delta_mix) and Hume-Rothery rules to estimate solid solution formation in HEAs, with specific thresholds for delta and mixing enthalpy.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In Reference [ [22] ], parameter δ is proposed to estimate the stabilization of solid solutions. The parameter specifies the difference between atom radii of the elements, and the following rules are formulated to determine the solid solution formation: −20 ≤ Δ H mix ≤ 5 kJ/mol, 12 ≤ Δ S mix ≤ 17.5 J/K·mol, δ ≤ 6.4%.

prior_approach.content: Later studies refined the critical value of delta and introduced a new thermodynamic parameter Omega combining mixing enthalpy, entropy, and average melting point.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Later in References [ [23] , [24] ], a critical value of the parameter δ was refined, and a more accurate thermodynamic parameter Ω was proposed. This parameter specifies the influence of mixing enthalpy and entropy and average melting point T m of the elements.

prior_approach.content: Prior research established mechanical properties for refractory HEAs obtained by arc melting, showing compressive strengths of 1270 and 2000 MPa.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Prior research shows the mechanical properties of the refractory NbMoWVTa [ [5] ] and NbMoWVTaTi [ [27] ] HEAs obtained by arc melting, where the compressive strength of the alloys are 1270 and 2000 MPa, respectively.

prior_limitation.content: Bulk samples of CrMoNbWV HEA had not previously been obtained.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: bulk samples of a CrMoNbWV high-entropy alloy (HEA) were obtained for the first time

prior_limitation.content: These refractory high-entropy alloys are brittle at room temperature, limiting their application as structural materials.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: On the other hand, these alloys are brittle at room temperature, leading to significant limitations of their application as structural materials.

causal_claim.content: Intensive mechanical impact caused diffraction peak broadening.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The diffraction peak broadening was caused by a decrease in the size of coherent scattering regions and increased internal stresses due to intensive mechanical impact during the MA.

causal_claim.content: Separation of elements with small atomic radii led to a decrease in lattice parameter.
causal_claim.evidence_span: its parameter slightly decreases (a = 3.106 Å) due to the separation of elements with small atomic radii (Cr, Fe, V) in the Laves phases and oxides.

causal_claim.content: Increase in sintering temperature decreased Cr2Nb content.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase in the sintering temperature led to a decrease in the Cr 2 Nb content.

causal_claim.content: Increase in sintering temperature decreased the volume fraction of Laves phases.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase of the sintering temperature led to a gradual decrease in the calculated volume fraction of the Laves phases

causal_claim.content: Interaction with carbon led to carburization of the surface layer.
causal_claim.evidence_span: under SPS, the HEA powder interacted with the carbon of the equipment that led to carburization of the surface layer

causal_claim.content: Carbon intercalation led to strains in the lattice and formation of carbides.
causal_claim.evidence_span: under sintering, carbon atoms were intercalated to the HEA BCC-lattice that led to strains in the latter and the formation of some HEA carbides.

causal_claim.content: Crystallization and localization of brittle phases promoted crack initiation and propagation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These phases were brittle at room temperature, and their localization promoted a crack initiation and propagation along the grain boundaries resulting in a decrease of the HEA plasticity.

causal_claim.content: Coarse oxide inclusions acted as crack initiation sources causing fractures.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The coarse inclusions can act as a crack initiation source and cause fractures in the BCC-matrix that leads to a decrease of the HEA plasticity.

causal_claim.content: Growth of BCC-matrix grains led to a decrease of hardness.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Figure 2 shows a growth of the BCC-matrix grains accompanies the increase in the sintering temperature, leading to a decrease of the hardness.

causal_claim.content: Increase in SPS temperature provided a positive shift of E OCP and decreased i corr.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase of the SPS temperature provided a positive shift of the E OCP and a decrease of i corr

causal_claim.content: Positive shift in E OCP and decrease in i corr led to good corrosion resistance.
causal_claim.evidence_span: leading to the good corrosion resistance of the SPS samples obtained at 1300–1400 °C, in H 2 SO 4 solution.

causal_claim.content: Increase in SPS temperature resulted in decreased i corr in the carburized layer.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The SPS temperature increase resulted in a decrease of i corr

causal_claim.content: The small atomic radius of chromium explains why Laves phases form in comparison to other refractory elements.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It is reported that the Laves phases are also formed in some other Cr-containing high-entropy alloys [ [2] , [14] , [15] ]. The smaller atomic radius of Cr can explain that in comparison to the other refractory elements.

causal_claim.content: Increasing the SPS temperature causes the reverse dissolution of Laves phases, likely due to the entropy component dominating the enthalpy component.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase of the SPS temperature leads to reverse dissolution of the Laves phases in the solid solution that is possibly connected with the higher influence of entropy component Δ S mix than the enthalpy one Δ H mix in this case.

causal_claim.content: The hexagonal, incoherent lattice of the precipitated oxides causes high strength but also results in brittleness.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In addition, the precipitated oxides have a hexagonal lattice that is incoherent to the CrMoNbWV HEA BCC-matrix. It leads to the high strength of the material but simultaneously to the brittleness as well.

causal_claim.content: Increasing SPS temperature reduces Laves phase content, while coarsening the grains leads to higher wear.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase of the SPS temperature results in a decrease of the Laves phase content in the samples. The Laves phase grains coarsen, leading to higher wear under the tests.

causal_claim.content: Sliding wear resistance is proportional to alloy hardness, as indicated by the Archard wear equation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: According to the equation, sliding wear resistance is proportional to the alloy hardness.

causal_claim.content: The increase in sintering temperature leads to an increase in carbon content due to higher diffusion from the graphite crucible.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The increase in sintering temperature leads to increases of C due to a higher diffusion of C from the graphite crucible.

mechanism_principle.content: The increase in sintering temperature promotes higher diffusion of elements within the alloy.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In addition, the increase of the sintering temperature promotes a higher diffusion of elements in the alloy.

mechanism_principle.content: Grain boundary hardening occurs because the SPS process results in a fine-grained structure with equiaxial grains smaller than 15 µm.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Compared to a coarse-grained structure of the HEA obtained by melting, the CrMoNbWV HEA, obtained by SPS of the MA-powder, has a structure with equiaxial grains with a size of less than 15 µm. This fact provides the grain boundary hardening of the BCC-matrix.

mechanism_principle.content: Dispersed Laves phases and oxides act as barriers to dislocation motion, increasing strength.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The Laves phases and oxides, formed under the SPS, are dispersed in the matrix and serve as barriers for dislocation motions.

mechanism_principle.content: Fine-grained Laves phases protect the surface from plastic deformation while the BCC solid solution protects against brittle fracture.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Simultaneously, the presence of the fine-grained Laves phases protects the surface from strong plastic deformations and prevents destructions during a sliding, while the BCC solid solution of high plasticity protects the surface from a brittle fracture.

mechanism_principle.content: The higher characteristics of the carburized layer result from lattice strain caused by carbon intercalation and the presence of fine-dispersed carbides.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The higher characteristics of the carburized layer probably result from the BCC-lattice strain caused by the intercalation of carbon atoms and the fine-dispersed HEA carbides.

mechanism_principle.content: Niobium's resistance to acids is explained by the formation of a thin, dense protective film that prevents direct interaction with the solution.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Despite the relatively high negative standard potential of niobium, its inertness to acids can be explained by forming a thin dense protective film on its surface, and this film prevents a direct interaction between the metal and the solution.

mechanism_principle.content: The formation of fine-dispersed carbides likely causes gradual dissolution of alloy components and the absence of a passivation region.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The formation of the fine-dispersed carbides in the samples probably provides the gradual dissolution of the alloy components and the almost total absence of the passivation region Δ E .

hypothesis_statement.content: The calculated thermodynamic parameters indicate that a single-phase solid solution is expected to form in the CrMoNbWV alloy.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The values in Table 7 find good agreement with the criteria mentioned above. Therefore a single-phase solid solution is expected to be formed in the CrMoNbWV alloy.

hypothesis_statement.content: Based on the calculated average valence electron concentration (VEC), a BCC solid solution is expected to form.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: According to the calculations ( Table 7 ), if VEC for CrMoNbWV is 5.6, that suggests BCC solid solution formation.

evidence_result.content: Sintering at 1400 °C caused BCC grain coarsening and reduced Laves phase content.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The temperature increase to 1400 °C led to a grain coarsening of the BCC phase and decreased the Laves phase content

evidence_result.content: Sintered samples exhibited high hardness and compressive strength at room temperature.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The sintered samples showed high hardness and compressive strength (2700–2800 MPa) at room temperature.

evidence_result.content: Wear tests showed excellent performance compared to conventional composites.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The wear tests demonstrated excellent results in comparison to conventional wear-resistant composites.

evidence_result.content: Samples showed high corrosion resistance in H2SO4 solution.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The obtained samples also exhibited high corrosion resistance under electrochemical tests in H 2 SO 4 solution.

evidence_result.content: CrMoNbWV HEA has comparable properties to WNbMoTaV but with reduced density.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The CrMoNbWV HEA has comparable mechanical and corrosive properties with the WNbMoTaV type HEA, but at the same time has a reduced density: CrMoNbWV—10.55 g/cm 3 , WNbMoTaV—12.42 g/cm 3 .

evidence_result.content: Mechanical alloying enabled the formation of a CrMoNbWV alloy with a single-phase BCC structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In the present paper, the MA allowed to obtain a CrMoNbWV alloy with a single-phase BCC structure.

evidence_result.content: Spark plasma sintering caused partial decomposition of the solid solution and precipitation of Laves phases and oxides.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, the following SPS leads to partial decomposition of the solid solution and precipitation of the Laves phases (Cr 2 Nb, (Cr, Fe)Nb) and oxides (NbVO 4 -VO).

evidence_result.content: Samples obtained by powder metallurgy (MA and SPS) showed significantly higher compressive strengths (3472 and 3834 MPa) compared to those from melting methods.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Refractory HEAs NbMoWVTa [ [19] ] and NbMoWVTaCr [ [2] ] obtained by MA and SPS showed higher compressive strengths of 3472 and 3834 MPa.

evidence_result.content: The synthesized CrMoNbWV HEA exhibited high corrosion resistance, hardness, and wear resistance.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The synthesized CrMoNbWV HEA exhibited high corrosion resistance, hardness, and wear resistance.
